title: Therapeutic Deep Eutectic System-Based PLGA In Situ Forming Implant for Rapid-Onset, Long-Acting Risperidone Delivery: In Vitro and In Vivo Evaluation
content: Background/Objectives: Schizophrenia requires long-term antipsychotic treatment, yet poor adherence to oral therapy remains a major challenge. Risperdal Consta® has been approved as a long-acting injectable risperidone (RISP) formulation to reduce dosing frequency and enhance patient compliance. However, this product exhibits a long initial lag phase in drug release, necessitating the co-administration of oral supplementation. To sort out this problem, this study aimed to develop a therapeutic deep eutectic system (THEDES)-based poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) in situ forming implant (ISFI) to avoid lag phase while maintaining long-acting release profiles. Additionally, THEDES allows the incorporation of RISP in a soluble form rather than suspended powder as occurs in almost all other conventional formulations, making formulation easier and more attractive for industrial translation. Methods: A THEDES composed of RISP and capric acid (CA) at a 3:7 molar ratio was incorporated into PLGA-based formulations with or without N-vinyl-2-pyrrolidone (NVP). Six formulations were screened for phase inversion and implant formation. F6, containing 0.50 mL THEDES, 0.40 g PLGA, and 1.0 mL NVP, formed a homogeneous precursor and a uniform, consolidated implant after aqueous exposure. Accordingly, F6 was selected and further evaluated by SEM, XRD, FTIR, rheological analysis, syringeability, Hansen solubility parameters, and partition coefficient. Drug release was assessed in vitro for 30 days, and in vivo for 83 days following administration of F6, THEDES, or Risperdal Consta® in rats. Results: F6 showed favorable PLGA compatibility, and 89.51 ± 0.41% extrudability. THEDES formation increased the apparent log P of RISP from 2.194 to 3.704 at pH 7.2. SEM showed a porous polymeric matrix, while XRD indicated a predominantly non-crystalline state of RISP. In vitro release of RISP from Risperdal Consta® exhibited a prolonged lag phase, with relatively low drug release during the first 20 days, followed by a marked increase thereafter. In contrast, F6 exhibited no apparent lag phase, with a progressive increase in drug release. A similar trend was observed in vivo as F6 showed earlier release than Risperdal Consta®, and maintained detectable risperidone concentrations through Day 83. Conclusions: These findings support THEDES-based PLGA ISFIs as a promising approach for a lag-free prolonged RISP delivery.
